fixes.explanation: Phinehas is a fine name, friend, but he isn't in this verse. The priest in the scene is Eleazar. The text says the daughters "…approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders…" (Joshua 17:4) Easy to grab a priest name off the shelf like the wrong-shaped cutter in a drawer full of them. Check the verse and Eleazar is right there.

That's right. The daughters say, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." (Joshua 17:4) They don't just ask. They point to what the LORD already commanded. Five daughters, one command, and they walked in carrying it like a recipe they knew by heart.

Yes, baker! The text says, "…the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh." (Joshua 17:6) The daughters got their inheritance among Manasseh's sons, and Gilead stayed with the rest of those sons. Think of Gilead as the big batch set out beyond the Jordan, a separate tray from the ten shares in verse 5. Keep your eyes on the trays and you're golden.

Gates, friend? Nice try, but no gates in this verse. The sons of Joseph say the Canaanites "…have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel." (Joshua 17:16) Iron chariots. Picture that one word and it sticks.
